_comment: Doctrine lint config (checked by Util/check_doctrine.py = ctest
doctrine_lint). Four independent source-hygiene gates the project brief
mandates; each has its own scope + suppression section here, each fails on
a NEW offence and carries its existing backlog as visible data (the
Util/ogre_containment.json model). Adding a sanctioned exception means
editing THIS file, with a reason, in the same change - the review speed
bump the lints exist for.
Raw ORKIGE_LUA/ORKIGE_NOSCRIPT preprocessor use is allowed ONLY in the
meta seam: the Meta.h backend selector, its two backends, and the
ScriptRuntime implementation. Everything else selects a backend through
the OMETA/OUSERTYPE macros, complete in both backends by design.
Competing game-engine and third-party product names must not appear in
code comments, string literals or Docs prose (identifiers are not
scanned). This table is the ONE sanctioned place for the names. The
project's OWN stack (OGRE/Ogre-Next, SDL, Jolt, vcpkg, ImGui, sol2, Lua,
OpenAL, Emscripten, WebGL, Metal, Vulkan, Lottie, ...) is never listed.
exempt_files carries vendored third-party sources (whose own docs may
mention anything) and the factual DevicePreset device table (real phone
model names are platform-target data, not a product comparison).
Ratified funnel doctrine (2026-07-23): core+engine runtime content reads
route through core_filesystem/ResourceReader so a mounted APK/pak
resolves in place with no extraction. Migration is incomplete; this
GATES - the funnel plumbing (the reader impl + the archive backends) is
allowed, every current raw-fs offender sits in `legacy` (visible
backlog), and a NEW raw-fs call in an unlisted core/engine file fails.
As call sites migrate, their legacy entry goes stale (= a lint failure)
and is removed, so the backlog can only shrink. Editor/tools/tests are
out of the runtime funnel's scope and not scanned here.

the funnel's archive backend - MiniZip reads pak/APK bytes in place; this IS the plumbing core_filesystem/ResourceReader resolves through
funnel_files.orkige_core/core_filesystem/FileWriter.c: the funnel's WRITE plumbing - the streaming, temp-then-rename file sink core writers go through (ResourceReader covers reads only); this IS the one place a core/engine writer opens a file, so the legacy writers above have a single call site to migrate onto

_comment: Every .h/.cpp/.mm in the core + engine libraries, tools, tests and
samples carries the standard header block (the 'part of orkige' notice
line + 'copyright: (c) 2009-2026 orkitec'). third_party carries vendored
sources that keep their own upstream licence header; generated files stay
generator-shaped and are sanctioned individually.

third_party.orkige_core/core_util/FastDelegate.h: vendored FastDelegate (Don Clugston, CodeProject) - keeps its upstream notice
third_party.orkige_core/core_util/MacroRepeat.h: vendored MacroRepeat (Robert Geiman, 2004) - keeps its upstream notice
third_party.orkige_core/core_util/ObjectFactory.h: vendored ObjectFactory (Robert Geiman, 2004) - keeps its upstream notice
third_party.tools/editor/IconsFontAwesome6.h: vendored IconFontCppHeaders glyph table (zlib licence) - keeps its upstream notice
third_party.tools/editor/GeneratedLuaApi.h: generated by Util/update_docs.py - must stay byte-exact generator output, no header block
